perspective:
**Mason Hurley’s available information:**

- Mason is an accountant at a small community center and knows Martha Moua as a personal care aide colleague there; their interactions are mainly work-related.
- While reviewing financial reports, Mason notices discrepancies: healthcare expenses look unusually high and inconsistent with usual spending patterns. He suspects Martha might be mismanaging funds and feels suspicious and anxious.
- Mason asks Martha to discuss the financial report. Martha says there is likely a reasonable explanation and asks what discrepancies he means. Mason points to the healthcare expenses. Martha says she sees the issue, thinks there may have been a misentry, and says she will review and correct errors.
- After reviewing with Martha, Mason understands the discrepancies were due to a clerical error, not mismanagement. He feels relieved and embarrassed.
- Mason apologizes to Martha for his initial suspicion and says he should have asked her first. Martha says it is okay, understands he was being thorough, and suggests double-checking entries next time.
- Mason comes to believe Martha is competent. He thinks recurring clerical errors indicate the financial management system is inadequate. He feels frustrated with the system but empathetic toward Martha.
- Mason tells Martha the issue is not her management but the current system. He proposes a new, more robust financial system, says he will draft a proposal, and asks for her input. Martha agrees and offers to help.
- Mason drafts the proposal and believes it will benefit operations, but he is uncertain whether management will approve or implement it.
- Mason tells Martha about his uncertainty. Martha says it is a solid proposal and encourages presenting it confidently. Mason decides to prepare a detailed presentation and asks Martha to help gather data; she agrees.
- Mason presents the proposal to management. He feels the presentation went well, feels satisfied but exhausted, and believes he has done everything he can. He knows the decision is now up to management.
- Mason tells Martha this. Martha praises his work and suggests taking time off. Mason thanks her, plans/takes a few days off to recharge and reflect, and hopes for good news. Martha tells him to enjoy the break and to let her know if he needs anything.
